title: The Story So Far
excerpt: Catching up on The Last Voyage before The Great Rift arrives November 3rd — where to find both books, and a spoiler-filled recap if you need one.
body:
You may be wondering, "Can I read The Great Rift without reading The Last Voyage first?" The answer is yes, of course. I wrote The Great Rift so you'll get the necessary background in the first few chapters. But I think you'll enjoy both books more by reading them as a pair. (Ethnogenesis, the third volume, will come out in 2027.)

Here are links, for print, ebook, and audiobook.
[The Last Voyage](https://www.amazon.com/dp/1399814141)
[The Great Rift](https://www.amazon.com/dp/1399838784?lv=shuf&channelId=500&plpRedirect=mhFallback)

Here's a recap of The Last Voyage if you need it, but be forewarned: this recap contains spoilers that you would probably rather discover for yourself ...

+++++ SPOILER ALERT +++++

It's 2056, and Earth is being pushed toward collapse, not just by ecological and economic breakdown, but also by rival international oligarchs who are quietly engineering a global crisis they intend to profit from. Two people are let in on this secret: Thurman Howard Thurman and Ekaterina Deripaska. They run Macopro, a company that has been quietly launching voyages to Mars in order to build an Assurance Colony there, a small, fragile foothold for humanity in case Earth's human population doesn't make it. When they learn what the oligarchs are planning, they realize there's no more time left. This will be the last voyage.

A unique crew is chosen for the mission:
**Colfax Innis** — a widowed environmental scientist and former head of the American EPA, recruited for his expertise in ecology (and in spite of his sharp tongue)
**Eve Innis** — Colfax's daughter, a scholar of ethics and comparative religion, brought on for a reason Macopro has kept quiet: a wave of suicides has broken out at the colony already on Mars, and no one can explain why
**Dei-Lin Wu** — a former Air Force officer turned botanist and plant pathologist, serving as co-pilot
**Ikemba Kalu** — a decorated Nigerian fighter pilot, the only crew member with prior spaceflight experience
**Soraya Rasul** — an entomologist studying the global pollinator collapse, appointed captain of the crew
**Gabriela Mercedes Coroy** — a geneticist from Guatemala, serving as first mate and crew medic
**Nikau Ruka** — once the frontperson of a chart-topping band, now a music and art therapist for traumatized children
**Refa Barghouthi** — a young musician and poet, the youngest person ever recruited for a Macopro crew

Two more spots are meant for a robotics expert and a computer systems expert, but on the eve of launch, both are kidnapped and never recovered. In the end, it's Thurman and Kat themselves who take those final two seats, stepping away from the lives and power they've built on Earth to join the crew they have assembled.

As the Ark carries its ten passengers into the 270-day journey to Mars, Eve and her colleagues begin investigating the suicides, unsure what they'll find when they finally arrive on the Red Planet. The Last Voyage thrusts ten strangers together in close quarters, on short notice, as they sort out what to hold onto and what to let go of, as they struggle to become something more than the world they left behind.

That's where The Great Rift begins: the Ark still en route, and word reaching the crew of just how much worse the situation at Mars Base has become.
